arxiv-1311-2807.title: Stability of germanene under tensile strain
arxiv-1311-2807.creator: T. P. Kaloni and U. Schwingenschlögl
arxiv-1311-2807.description: A 2013 arXiv research paper by T. P. Kaloni and U. Schwingenschlögl. The stability of germanene under biaxial tensile strain and electronic properties are studied by means of density functional theory based calculations. Our results show that up to 16% biaxial tensile strain germanene lattice is stable and the Dirac cone shifts towards higher energy range with respect to the Fermi level as a result p p -doped Dirac states are achieved.

arxiv-2109-00397.title: Graph Automorphism Shuffles from Pile-Scramble Shuffles
arxiv-2109-00397.creator: Kengo Miyamoto, Kazumasa Shinagawa
arxiv-2109-00397.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Kengo Miyamoto, Kazumasa Shinagawa. A pile-scramble shuffle is one of the most effective shuffles in card-based cryptography. Indeed, many card-based protocols are constructed from pile-scramble shuffles. This article aims to study the power of pile-scramble shuffles. In particular, for any directed graph G G , we introduce a new protocol called “a graph shuffle protocol for G G ”, and show that it can be implemented by using pile-scramble shuffles only.

arxiv-2109-07701.title: SPIN Road Mapper: Extracting Roads from Aerial Images via Spatial and Interaction Space Graph Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
arxiv-2109-07701.creator: Wele Gedara Chaminda Bandara, Jeya Maria Jose Valanarasu, Vishal M. Patel
arxiv-2109-07701.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Wele Gedara Chaminda Bandara, Jeya Maria Jose Valanarasu, Vishal M. Patel. Road extraction is an essential step in building autonomous navigation systems. Detecting road segments is challenging as they are of varying widths, bifurcated throughout the image, and are often occluded by terrain, cloud, or other weather conditions. Using just convolution neural networks (ConvNets) for this problem is not effective as it is inefficient at capturing distant dependencies between road segments in the image which is essential to extract road connectivity.

arxiv-2112-01264.title: Thermodynamics of galaxy clusters in modified Newtonian potential
arxiv-2112-01264.creator: Abdul W. Khanday, Sudhaker Upadhyay, Prince A. Ganai
arxiv-2112-01264.description: Abstract We study the thermodynamics of galaxy clusters in a modified Newtonian potential motivated by a general solution to Newton’s “sphere-point” equivalence theorem. We obtain the N N particle partition function by evaluating the configurational integral while accounting for the extended nature of galaxies (via the inclusion of the softening parameter ϵ \epsilon into the potential energy function).

arxiv-2205-00336.title: A nonparametric regression alternative to empirical Bayes approaches to simultaneous estimation
arxiv-2205-00336.creator: Alton Barbehenn, Sihai Dave Zhao
arxiv-2205-00336.description: Abstract The simultaneous estimation of multiple unknown parameters lies at heart of a broad class of important problems across science and technology. Currently, the state-of-the-art performance in the such problems is achieved by nonparametric empirical Bayes methods. However, these approaches still suffer from two major issues.

arxiv-2211-07635.title: Learnable Spatio-Temporal Map Embeddings for Deep Inertial Localization
arxiv-2211-07635.creator: Dennis Melamed, Karnik Ram, Vivek Roy, Kris Kitani
arxiv-2211-07635.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Dennis Melamed, Karnik Ram, Vivek Roy, Kris Kitani. Indoor localization systems often fuse inertial odometry with map information via hand-defined methods to reduce odometry drift, but such methods are sensitive to noise and struggle to generalize across odometry sources. To address the robustness problem in map utilization, we propose a data-driven prior on possible user locations in a map by combining learned spatial map embeddings and temporal odometry embeddings.

arxiv-2211-09589.title: Superfluid drain vortex
arxiv-2211-09589.creator: Wandrille Ruffenach, Luca Galantucci, Carlo F. Barenghi
arxiv-2211-09589.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Wandrille Ruffenach, Luca Galantucci, Carlo F. Barenghi. Drain vortices are among the most common vortices observed in everyday life, yet their physics is complex due to the competition of vorticity’s transport and diffusion, and the presence of viscous layers and a free surface. Recently, it has become possible to study experimentally drain vortices in superfluid liquid helium, a fluid in which the physics is simplified by the absence of viscosity and the quantisation of the circulation.

arxiv-2406-16064.title: MicroMagnetic.jl: A Julia package for micromagnetic and atomistic simulations with GPU support
arxiv-2406-16064.creator: Weiwei Wang, Boyao Lyu, Lingyao Kong, Hans Fangohr, Haifeng Du
arxiv-2406-16064.description: Abstract MicroMagnetic.jl is an open-source Julia package for micromagnetic and atomistic simulations. Using the features of the Julia programming language, MicroMagnetic.jl supports CPU and various GPU platforms, including NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and Apple GPUs. Moreover, MicroMagnetic.jl supports Monte Carlo simulations for atomistic models and implements the Nudged-Elastic-Band method for energy barrier computations.

arxiv-2407-13602.title: Actions of large finite groups on aspherical manifolds
arxiv-2407-13602.creator: Jordi Daura Serrano
arxiv-2407-13602.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jordi Daura Serrano. In this paper we study actions of finite groups on closed connected aspherical manifolds. Under some assumptions on the outer automorphism group of the fundamental group of a closed connected aspherical manifold M M , we prove that the homeomorphism group of M M is Jordan, we bound the discrete degree of symmetry of M M and obtain a rigidity result, and we study the number of stabilizers of finite group actions on M M .

arxiv-2408-10781.title: C 2 C^{2} estimates for k k -Hessian equations and a rigidity theorem
arxiv-2408-10781.creator: RUIJIA ZHANG
arxiv-2408-10781.description: Abstract . We derive a concavity inequality for k k -Hessian operators under the semi-convexity condition. As an application, we establish interior estimates for semiconvex solutions to the k k -Hessian equations with vanishing Dirichlet boundary conditions and obtain a Liouville-type result.

arxiv-2411-14978.title: Hyperons in neutron star mergers
arxiv-2411-14978.creator: Andreas Bauswein
arxiv-2411-14978.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Andreas Bauswein. We discuss the effects induced by the potential presence of hyperons in hot and ultra-dense matter within the context of neutron star mergers. Specifically, we address their effect on the dominant post-merger frequency of the gravitational waves. By performing a simulation campaign with a large sample of hyperonic and nucleonic equations of state, we explicitly show that the unique thermal behavior of hyperonic equations of state results in a systematic shift of the dominant frequency with respect to the nucleonic reference level.

arxiv-2502-04035.title: Complete FSM Testing Using Strong Separability
arxiv-2502-04035.creator: Robert M. Hierons, Mohammad Reza Mousavi
arxiv-2502-04035.description: Abstract Apartness is a concept developed in constructive mathematics, which has resurfaced as a powerful notion for separating states in the area of model learning and model-based testing. We identify some fundamental shortcomings of apartness in quantitative models, such as in hybrid and stochastic systems.

arxiv-2509-02993.title: SPENet: Self-guided Prototype Enhancement Network for Few-shot Medical Image Segmentation
arxiv-2509-02993.creator: Chao Fan, Xibin Jia, Anqi Xiao, Hongyuan Yu, Zhenghan Yang, Dawei Yang, Hui Xu, Yan Huang, Liang Wang
arxiv-2509-02993.description: Abstract Few-Shot Medical Image Segmentation (FSMIS) aims to segment novel classes of medical objects using only a few labeled images. Prototype-based methods have made significant progress in addressing FSMIS. However, they typically generate a single global prototype for the support image to match with the query image, overlooking intra-class variations.

arxiv-2510-01428.title: BioVERSE : Representation Alignment of Biomedical Modalities to LLMs for Multi-Modal Reasoning
arxiv-2510-01428.creator: Ching-Huei Tsou, Michal Ozery-Flato, Ella Barkan, Diwakar Mahajan, Ben Shapira
arxiv-2510-01428.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ching-Huei Tsou, Michal Ozery-Flato, Ella Barkan, Diwakar Mahajan, Ben Shapira. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and biomedical foundation models (BioFMs) have achieved strong results in biological text reasoning, molecular modeling, and single-cell analysis, yet they remain siloed in disjoint embedding spaces, limiting cross-modal reasoning. We present BioVERSE ( Bio medical V ector E mbedding R ealignment for S emantic E ngagement), a two-stage approach that adapts pretrained BioFMs as modality encoders and aligns them with LLMs through lightweight, modality-specific projection layers.
